subject: Physics
description: Radioactivity, atomic structure, nuclear fission/fusion, famous experiments

questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel (1896) discovered radioactivity in uranium salts accidentally — they fogged a photographic plate kept in a drawer. Marie and Pierre Curie later isolated polonium and radium. Rutherford identified alpha, beta rays. Röntgen discovered X-rays (1895). Nobel Physics 1903 shared: Becquerel + Curies.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The three radioactive emissions (in order of penetrating power, least to greatest) are:
questions.explanation: Alpha (helium nucleus, +2) — stopped by paper. Beta (fast electron, −1) — stopped by aluminium sheet. Gamma (high-energy EM) — needs thick lead or concrete. Ionising power is the REVERSE order (alpha most ionising, gamma least).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The famous mass-energy equivalence relation is:
questions.explanation: Einstein's 1905 special relativity — E = mc². Tiny mass converts to enormous energy (c² ≈ 9 × 10¹⁶ J/kg). Basis for nuclear fission (atom bomb, reactors) and fusion (Sun, stars, H-bomb).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The source of the SUN's energy is:
questions.explanation: Sun fuses hydrogen into helium in its core (proton-proton chain, ~15 million K). 620 million tonnes H → He every second, losing ~4.3 million tonnes as energy (E=mc²). Fusion = combining nuclei. Fission = splitting heavy nuclei (U-235, Pu-239 in reactors/bombs).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The PHOTOELECTRIC EFFECT (for which Einstein won Nobel 1921) demonstrated that:

options.option_text: Light has particle (photon) nature — exists in quanta of energy hν

questions.explanation: Einstein 1905: light acts as particles (photons) with energy E = hν. Explained why photoelectric emission depends on FREQUENCY, not intensity. Kicked off quantum mechanics. (Matter-wave hypothesis came from de Broglie 1924; nuclear discovery from Rutherford 1911.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The ATOMIC NUCLEUS was discovered by Ernest Rutherford in his famous:
questions.explanation: Rutherford (1911) — fired alpha particles at thin gold foil. Most passed through; a few bounced back sharply. Concluded the positive charge is concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus. J.J. Thomson — cathode rays → electron. Millikan — oil-drop (electron charge).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The CERN LARGE HADRON COLLIDER (LHC) is located near the border of:
questions.explanation: LHC — 27 km underground ring at CERN, straddling the French-Swiss border near Geneva. In July 2012 LHC experiments (ATLAS + CMS) announced the discovery of the Higgs boson (Nobel 2013 for Higgs + Englert).
